title: Branch access and head-office approval conflict

retrieve_on.symptom_narrative: Head office pays and approves parts, but branches call and control access. Branches expect appointments before approval arrives. Equipment moves between similar-named locations. Several apparently separate failures turned out to follow one central configuration change.
retrieve_on.workflow_context: Maintenance provider for multi-site retail and education groups; one customer has 28 branches.

discriminating_questions.question: Who approves expenditure and access?
discriminating_questions.synthetic_answer: Head office approves cost; the branch agrees access.
discriminating_questions.branch_if_answer_differs: Similar symptoms across branches may be independent hardware faults; common timing is a hypothesis, not proof.

positive_mechanism: Customer hierarchy, device location and approval dependencies are not modelled consistently.
counterexample: Similar symptoms across branches may be independent hardware faults; common timing is a hypothesis, not proof.
minimum_evidence: A simulated move record conflicts with the asset sheet.
Simulated tickets share a configuration-change timestamp.
A simulated approval matrix separates branch and central authority.
process_intervention: Establish organization/site/device identities and separate access approval from spending approval; retain local child tickets under confirmed shared incidents.
automation_candidate: Link related incidents for review; route approvals to scoped authorities; provide role-filtered views and readiness checks.
unknowns: Organization hierarchy, approver limits and actual shared dependencies need confirmation.
stop_rule: If discriminating evidence is absent or conflicting, return an unresolved hypothesis plus a targeted question, not a confident solution.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Hierarchical incidents, effective asset locations and scoped approval routing are extensions.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.
